conviction_note: Nothing decisive found: the evidence is industry proxies (Vetsource visits -1.9% in Q3 against management's ~-1.5% H2 assumption, a dollar ~1-1.5% stronger than when the FY guide was set) leaning slightly negative, against a company that has beaten and raised every 2026 quarter, so p_up sits at 48 on a 7.5% absolute move, giving -0.3; the findings sum to -1.0 because they are sized one by one and not fitted to that number, and the gap is the proxies being small individually while the reaction function (0.0%, -4.6%, +3.6% on the three 2026 beat-and-raise prints) gives no reason to lean harder.

Company guide (Q2 call 2026-08-04, https://www.webull.com/news/15344824561263616): Q3 organic growth in line with the implied H2 range, Q3 reported operating margin 32.5-32.8%, Q3 FX ~70bp headwind to reported revenue; FY2026 revenue $4,700-4,745M, organic 8.5-9.7%, CAG recurring organic 9.5-10.7%, EPS $14.69-14.94, H2 US clinical visits ~-1.5% (8-K ex99.1 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000874716/000110465926090033/tm2622041d1_ex99-1.htm). My arithmetic: H1 2026 revenue $2,357M at 10.0% organic implies H2 organic ~7.1-9.4% (midpoint ~8.2%); the $1.19B consensus at +~7.7% reported plus ~0.7pt FX is ~8.4% organic, i.e. slightly above the guided midpoint. FY EPS consensus reported at $14.68, below the guide low end (single AI-generated source, treated as disputed).

findings.finding: Vetsource data (CATalyst Council release 2026-10-13, reported by dvm360 2026-10-23, 6,595 US practices) show all-species US clinical visits down 1.9% YoY in Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep), canine down and puppy visits -10%, feline +2.7%; management's H2 assumption on the Q2 call was ~-1.5% US clinical visits after a -1.3% Q2 on IDEXX's own same-store measure, so this industry series sits ~0.4pt worse than the planning assumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Visits are the line this name has traded on in 2026: the Q4 2025 print (2026-02-02) beat and guided above estimates but the stock fell -4.6% on a cautious ~-2% visits assumption; Q2 (2026-08-04) reported -1.3% visits with a 10% organic recurring beat and the stock rose +3.6%. A visits headwind has been absorbed by price (~4%) and test intensity in every 2026 quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a trade-press series rather than a wire item, and IDEXX measures visits on its own panel with a different definition, so the street's -1.5% assumption is the company's; if the -1.9% were priced, Q3 revenue consensus would sit at or below the guided H2 midpoint rather than slightly above it (~8.4% organic vs ~8.2%), and the 20-day run-up of +8.4% into the print argues the market is not leaning on visit weakness. Caveat sized in: Vetsource and IDEXX's panel differ, the Q2 Vetsource comparable is not cleanly sourced (the July release gives -1.50% for the twelve months to June), and feline growth (+2.7%) favours diagnostic intensity.
findings.independence: Management's own H2 assumption on the Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/idexx-laboratories-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-04/) is the comparison, not corroboration. Merck Animal Health's Q3 companion animal +6% ex-FX (finding 2) is a different, product-driven series and neither confirms nor contradicts visits. Proxy: macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by IDEXX.

findings.finding: Merck's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-29), the only vet-channel counterparty to report since IDEXX last spoke, shows companion animal sales $628M, +6% ex-FX, 'largely driven by new product launches', with Bravecto flat ex-FX, after +7% in Q2 and +9% in Q1 2026: a vet-channel read that is steady-to-slightly-decelerating and silent on visits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved instance of IDXX reacting to a Merck Animal Health read; the name's prints are driven by its own CAG recurring growth and guidance (+14.8% Nov 2025, +27.5% Aug 2025 on raises).
findings.why_not_priced: Published three sessions before the print inside a $17bn pharma release; Animal Health is a small line nobody previews IDEXX on. If it had been read as a vet-channel slowdown, animal-health names would have sold off on 2026-10-29/30; the baseline 5-day run-up of +0.3% shows no such move in IDXX. It is a weak, product-mix-driven proxy for an IDEXX diagnostics quarter, so small.
findings.independence: Different source from finding 1 (Vetsource) and points weakly the same way (deceleration from +9% to +7% to +6%). Zoetis reports 2026-11-05, after the window (https://investor.zoetis.com/news/news-details/2026/Zoetis-to-Host-Webcast-and-Conference-Call-on-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx).

findings.finding: The dollar has strengthened since IDEXX set its FY guide on 2026-08-04: DXY ~100.3-100.8 at end-July (Cambridge Currencies / Convex estimates) against 101.81-101.87 on 2026-10-23/26 (RTTNews), roughly 1-1.5%; IDEXX's stated sensitivity is ~$8M of revenue per 1% stronger dollar for the rest of the year, so the reported FY revenue guide carries an ~$8-12M FX cut (about 0.2%), the same mechanism that took $15M off the guide in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-04 an organic raise was netted by a $15M FX cut, leaving the revenue midpoint +$5M; the stock rose +3.6% on the EPS raise. FX-driven trims have not been the deciding line in the 2026 reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The street usually updates FX in models, so this is likely partly priced; what is not priced is the headline optics: if the organic beat is ~$10M the reported revenue range may not rise at all, which is what a headline-driven open reacts to. If priced, revenue consensus ($1.19B) would sit at or below the guided midpoint rather than slightly above it. Small because ~0.2% of revenue and partly offsettable by margin.
findings.independence: Sensitivity from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15344824561263616); end-July DXY from https://cambridgecurrencies.com/us-dollar-index-dxy-forecast/ (estimate, not an ICE close). Independent of findings 1 and 2.

findings.finding: The FY2026 EPS consensus is reported at $14.68, one cent below the low end of IDEXX's own raised guide of $14.69-14.94 (and ~$0.13 below its midpoint), while the Q3 EPS whisper is $3.82 against a $3.71 consensus; a reaffirmed or raised EPS range therefore lands above the street's full-year number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS-guide raises bought +3.6% (Aug 2026), 0.0% (May 2026), +14.8% (Nov 2025) and +27.5% (Aug 2025); the 2026 reactions to raises have been muted.
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus below the company's own floor means the sell-side is haircutting the guide (FX, H2 spend); if the market fully trusted the guide the consensus would sit at the midpoint. Capped small: the $14.68 figure has one source, an AI-generated preview, and the whisper shows the buy-side already expects a beat.
findings.independence: Guide range from the company 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000874716/000110465926090033/tm2622041d1_ex99-1.htm). The FX finding (3) argues the haircut is partly justified; net of it this stays small.

findings.finding: Product cadence inside Q3 that feeds recurring revenue: Cancer Dx expanded in late September to a panel adding mast cell tumor detection at no price increase, with >20% of Cancer Dx orders from practices using a competitor's reference lab; inVue Dx FNA rollout began in Q3 toward broad availability by year-end (management: roughly doubles procedure volume for users); company on pace for 5,500 inVue placements in 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Innovation-driven recurring beats have been sold or ignored in 2026 (0.0% in May, -4.6% in Feb despite beats); they paid in 2025 (+27.5%, +14.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are company-disclosed and flagged in previews. What is not yet visible is the Q3 number (Cancer Dx clinic count, FNA uptake, competitive-lab wins); if the market credited it, recurring growth expectations would sit above the 9.5-10.7% guided range rather than inside it. Small, and inside what the company already guided.
findings.independence: Morgan Stanley conference summary 2026-09-14 (https://quartr.com/events/idexx-laboratories-idxx-morgan-stanley-24th-annual-global-healthcare-conference_3YkDXwfA) repeats the FNA and Cancer Dx points: same company, so one source.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 2026 reactions +3.57, -0.03, -4.60 against 2025's +14.84, +27.49, +8.95, +11.13; the name's response to good numbers has damped as the stock de-rated.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself price, so this is the bar rather than a mispricing; it is filed because a beat now has to clear an extra ~8% of anticipation. If the market were pricing disappointment, skew would be bid (it is +0.49, balanced) and the stock would not have recovered off the low. Sized small: the stock is still 27% off its high and the run-up may be valuation repair rather than earnings anticipation.
findings.independence: Spot and run-up from the sealed baseline; Oct 9 quote https://www.bloomberglinea.com/quote/IDXX:UN/ ; short interest https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/IDXX/short-interest/ .
